newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer plans new chemical plants in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Bayer plans new chemical plants in Thailand.

text.p: German chemical giant Bayer AG plans to invest around 500 million marks ($327 million) in building chemical facilities in Thailand in coming years with its Thai partner, Chemical Group of Companies, Bayer said on Wednesday.
The investment is aimed at meeting the demands of growing markets in Southeast-Asia, Bayer said.

Among the projects planned include a plant for making the polycarbonate Makrolon in Map Ta Phut in the province of Rayong for the middle of next year, which will produce 40,000 tonnes annually of polycarbonates from 1999.
The new plant will part of its Bayer Premier Polycarbonate Co Ltd (BPPC) subsidiary, of which Bayer owns 76 percent.
The co-operation between the German and Thai partners had been successful so far, the companies said.
